_comment: Переделка по замечаниям: у каждого слова принципиально другой заход, а не вариация прежней сцены.
tempo: a classic hourglass on a wooden desk, sand streaming through the narrow waist, warm side light, close-up
vez: a hand holding up exactly one index finger against a plain background, clear gesture meaning one time
moço(a): a young man and a young woman in their early twenties standing side by side outdoors, relaxed and smiling at the camera
pior: two apples side by side on a table, one fresh and shiny, the other rotten and brown, the rotten one in sharp focus
certo(a): a big bright green check mark drawn on a school notebook page by a teacher's hand
fácil: a hand effortlessly lifting a single white feather with two fingers, light and airy
ser: an open passport lying on a table with the photo page visible, identity document close-up
estar: a traveller with a suitcase standing on a railway platform, waiting, looking around
poder: strong hands easily twisting open a tightly sealed glass jar lid
achar: a delighted man picking up a coin he just found on the ground, holding it up
o/a: one single book pulled halfway out of a long row of identical books on a shelf
esta/este: an extreme close-up of a finger pointing directly at one specific cup standing on a table
maneiro: an excited young man in sunglasses giving an enthusiastic double thumbs up, delighted expression
tchau: a woman on a station platform waving goodbye to a departing train
médio: three apples in a row on a table, small, medium and large, the medium one in sharp focus and the others blurred
o mesmo: identical twin boys in matching clothes standing next to each other, looking at the camera
existe: a shopkeeper holding up a product from the shelf to show a customer that it is in stock
